learning_outcomes.text: Critically analyse the structural resistance of machine components, undergoing static and fatigue loads.
Analyse the mechanical behaviour of structures undergoing static or dynamic loads.
Calculate stresses and displacements in simple structural components (beams, shaft, etc.) and point out the corresponding safety margin.
Assess the structural resistance of mechanical components undergoing static, thermal and fatigue loads.
Size a mechanical component, considered as part of a complex assembly, in compliance with design constraints and technical norms.
Apply diagnosis techniques for failure mode assessment in a mechanical component and schedule the needed maintenance.

Analyse the damaging phenomena undermining in service functional performances of materials used in engineering applications, with allowance for their mutual interdependence, microstructure and applied heat/mechanical treatments.
Design a complex mechanical assembly, with consideration of all the previously mentioned aspects.

syllabus_topics: STRESS/STRAIN ASSESSMENT IN THREE-DIMENSIONAL CONFIGURATIONS OF BEAMS UNDERGOING STATIC LOADS.

STATIC FAILURE CRITERIA FOR BRITTLE AND DUCTILE MATERIALS, WITH ISOTROPIC CONSTITUTIVE LAW, FAILURE ASSESSMENT AND SIZING FOR STRUCTURAL COMPONENTS: DESIGN CRITERIA, SAFETY COEFFICIENTS, COMPLIANCE TO TECHNICAL STANDARDS.
BUCKLING, EULERIAN CRITICAL LOAD OMEGA METHOD
AXIAL-SYMMETRIC ELASTIC PROBLEMS: STRESS/STRAIN ASSESSMENT FOR PRESSURE VESSELS WITH THIN OR THICK WALLS.
UNIAXIAL AND MULTIAXIAL FATIGUE: EFFECT OF COMPONENT SIZE, SURFACE ROUGHNESS, NOTCHES; WHOLER CURVES.
CRITERIA AND NORMS FOR FATIGUE FALILURE ASSESSMENT AND SIZING.

FUNCTIONAL MODE, FAILURE ASSESSMENT AND SIZING OF: NON REMOVABLE (RIVETING, WELDING, BONDING) AND REMOVABLE JOINT COMPONENTS (COMPONENTS FIT TOGETHER, FEATHER KEY, TABS, SPLINED SHAFT, BOLTS, MANOUVRE AND POWER SCREW);
VISIT TO THE LABORATORY OF THE MACHINE DESIGN GROUP
assessment_rules: The exam is based on a written and an oral exam. The written test is based on the numerical resolution of an exercise on the verification/fatigue design of mechanical components or assemblies and is preparatory for access to the related oral test. The written test remains valid within the exam session in which it is passed. Among the minimum requirements for passing the exam, a relevant role is attributed to the ability to solve static and uniaxial and multiaxial fatigue of elementary structures, with reference to 'reasonable' numerical evaluations (e.g., serious errors of orders of magnitude are particularly serious, without the student noticing it, on the numerical questions proposed). The final grade is an average of the grades obtained in the two parts of the exam.
